best_for: Offices and family IT helpers who keep Thunderbird on many PCs and would rather meet new features once a year than every month.
description:
Thunderbird ESR is the extended support edition of Thunderbird, the free, open source email app started in 2003 and now part of the Mozilla family. Its developers work in a for-profit company owned by the nonprofit Mozilla, while the Thunderbird Council, elected by contributors since 2014, approves budgets and shapes the roadmap.

You can sort incoming mail with filters and change how the app looks. Thunderbird says it does not collect or store your personal data unless you ask it to, and that it will never sell it. If you also want your mail on your phone, Thunderbird makes an Android app, offered on Google Play and F-Droid.

points.title: New features once a year
points.text: ESR gets a feature update once a year and monthly stability and security fixes in between. The regular Release channel, which Mozilla recommends for most people, changes every month. ESR gives you fewer surprises in the interface and fewer chances for an add-on to break.

points.title: Same mail, calendar and chat
points.text: It is the same free, MPL-2.0 licensed Thunderbird, with mail, calendar, contacts, feeds and chat.

points.title: Add-ons can still break
points.text: Mozilla notes that every channel, ESR included, may not work with all add-ons. If you depend on one add-on, check that it supports the current ESR before a yearly jump.

points.title: Windows 10 and macOS 10.15 or later
points.text: The 153 ESR line needs Windows 10 or later (32-bit or 64-bit, 1 GB of RAM, 2 GB for 64-bit) or macOS 10.15 or later on Intel or Apple silicon. On Linux it is 64-bit only.

points.title: Windows installs for all users
points.text: The Windows installers here are machine-wide, in 32-bit and 64-bit builds, so you need administrator rights. The Mac download is one universal .dmg.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is Mozilla's own
points.text: The Flathub package is marked verified for MZLA Technologies, the Mozilla subsidiary behind Thunderbird. It is x64 only.

points.title: Downgrades: Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 71 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so going back there needs another source.
